title: Green watercress risotto with chicken and celeriac

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Everything is a plain whole food or a cupboard staple, including chicken stock, Parmesan and butter, with no jars, packets or substitutes.

supermarket.reason: Chicken thighs, leeks, celeriac, watercress, risotto rice and Parmesan are all everyday Tesco items at normal prices.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a wide pan and a ladle, and ladling stock into a risotto is well within a confident beginner's reach.

works.reason: 300g rice to 1.2 litres of stock with six thighs and 200g watercress is a sound ratio for four, and the chicken cooks through over the 30 minutes in the pan.

honest_times.reason: Dicing the chicken, peeling and dicing the celeriac, slicing the leeks, then 30 minutes of stirring adds up to roughly the 45 minutes printed in total, which is believable for a standard risotto.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning is used, including the thyme and the lemon, and nothing outside the lists appears apart from water.

seasonal_feel.reason: A warming risotto suits a mid-March evening, and the watercress is used generously, stalks cooked in and leaves wilted through, so it gives the dish its colour and flavour.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, plain British English that a neighbour could follow, with no restaurant language or health preaching.

hearty_healthy.reason: It is a proper family dinner with chicken, two vegetables, greens and rice, finished with a little butter and cheese.
